subject: Evidence handoff: syslog ingestion, KMS rotation notes & SIG mapping
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>
To: Brenna Holt <brenna.holt@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence handoff: syslog ingestion, KMS rotation notes & SIG mapping

Hi Brenna —

Following our sync earlier, attaching the materials you asked for to populate the OneTrust profile and to help your audit team validate log collection and key management controls. High-level summary below and ask at the end.

What’s attached
- redwood_syslog_architecture.png — network diagram showing our syslog collector topology (regional collectors, VPC peering, and IAM roles used for write-only ingestion).
- kms-rotation-playbook.pdf — internal playbook describing automatic rotation schedule, key versioning, and access control lists for customer-key-wrapping.
- SIG-response-mapping.xlsx — working sheet mapping SIG rows to CAIQ/SOC2 artifact buckets and the file names we’ll upload.

Notes / clarifications
1) Syslog retention: We retain structured logs (ingestion metadata + request traces) for 365 days in our encrypted S3 bucket (logs-redwood-prod-us). Raw system logs are rotated after 30 days unless flagged for incident retention.
2) Ingestion pipeline: Logs are forwarded from edge collectors to a centralized Fluentd fleet in the ingestion VPC, then delivered to S3 and to our observability cluster (CloudWatch/Datadog). TLS 1.2+ is enforced on all transport.
3) KMS model: We use customer-separable keys for private deployments (Customer-managed CMKs) and Redwood-managed master keys for hosted tenants. Rotation is automatic every 90 days for Redwood-managed keys; customer-managed keys follow the customer’s KMS policy.

Action items for Acme (requested)
- Please confirm whether your audit team needs a time-stamped sample of syslog events (we can provide a redacted 7-day window).
- Will you accept the SIG mapping spreadsheet as the primary crosswalk, or does the team prefer CAIQ-aligned JSON?
- Any preferred uploader for evidence (OneTrust portal link vs S3 presigned ingest)? We can push to OneTrust if you provide an upload token.

Thanks — looping Neha and Marissa for any missing artifacts.

—
Mateo Alvarez
Security Program Manager, Redwood Inference
mateo@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood_syslog_architecture.png (image/png), kms-rotation-playbook.pdf (application/pdf), SIG-response-mapping.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Brenna Holt <brenna.holt@acmecorp.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>
Cc: security-evidence@acmecorp.com
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 11:34:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Evidence handoff: syslog ingestion, KMS rotation notes & SIG mapping

Thanks Mateo — this is great and exactly the level of detail we needed. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

1) For the audit window we’d like a redacted 14-day sample of syslog events (UTC timestamps preferred). Redaction should remove any PII and customer-specific identifiers.
2) The auditor prefers the SIG mapping as an XLSX (your spreadsheet is fine) but will also ask for CAIQ output if we can auto-generate it from your mapping. If you can produce a CAIQ JSON export it will speed validation.
3) Upload preference: OneTrust is easiest for our reviewers. I can provision an upload token for your team and will send a separate secure link.

Two procedural asks — can you add a short statement in the KMS playbook about emergency key rollback steps (who is authorized, expected SLA for rollback, and audit trail retention)? Also please confirm whether rotation runs as a background job or as a manual runbook.

We’ll wait for the 14-day redacted log sample and the CAIQ JSON if possible.

Best,
Brenna
Brenna Holt
Information Security, AcmeCorp
brenna.holt@acmecorp.com

--- Original message forwarded ---

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Brenna Holt <brenna.holt@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evidence handoff: Evidence handoff: syslog ingestion, KMS rotation notes & SIG mapping

Brenna — quick update from our side after internal review:

- Redacted logs: we can generate the 14-day sample as requested. ETA: 2 business days to prepare redaction scripts and verification. Delivery mechanism: secure SFTP or presigned S3 link (let us know preference).
- KMS playbook: rotation is fully automated for Redwood-managed keys (cron-triggered rotation orchestrated by our key-service with audit events pushed to the audit S3 prefix). For customer-managed keys we document the recommended rotation cadence; we do not rotate customer-managed CMKs but we record rotation events if the customer triggers them.
- Emergency rollback: we will add an explicit section to kms-rotation-playbook.pdf covering emergency rollback: authorization list (Security Ops leads + CTO), rollback steps, and 180-day audit log retention for rollback actions. We’ll attach a diff to the updated playbook.

Open question for Acme: do you require raw ingestion configs (Fluentd config snippets) or is the architecture diagram and sample events sufficient?

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Director, Platform Security
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

Attachment: proposed-kms-diff.patch (text/plain)

From: Brenna Holt <brenna.holt@acmecorp.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>
Cc: security-evidence@acmecorp.com
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2027 16:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Evidence handoff: Evidence handoff: syslog ingestion, KMS rotation notes & SIG mapping

Neha, Mateo — thanks for the quick turn. This all looks good. A couple final points before we close the ticket: 

- OneTrust upload token: please use this secure uploader link (sent via separate secure email) to place the three artifacts and the redacted sample. If anything fails, reply-all and I’ll open a temporary S3 ingest.
- CAIQ: we didn’t require a strict JSON format but the auditor prefers machine-readable CAIQ. If you can export the SIG mapping to CAIQ JSON it will close 90% of the checklist. Otherwise we’ll manually map from the XLSX.
- Demo ask: our auditor would like a 20-minute Zoom to see the Fluentd -> S3 flow (screen-share of the ingestion dashboard and an explanation of the TLS-enforced transport). Can you propose two 20-minute slots tomorrow?

We’ll mark this as In Review once uploads complete. Appreciate the responsiveness — you’ve made this an easy review cycle.

Best,
Brenna

Attachment stubs referenced: redwood_syslog_architecture.png, kms-rotation-playbook.pdf, SIG-response-mapping.xlsx, redacted_syslog_sample-20270714-20270727.json (to be uploaded)
